subject: Media Literacy
title: Ownership and Corporate Bias
description: A fast breakdown of Ownership and Corporate Bias for builders.

hook.text: Six companies own 90% of US media. Their interests shape what 330 million Americans see and hear.

buildup.text: Media consolidation means a small number of corporations control most news, entertainment, and information.

discovery.text: When a parent company has interests in defense, pharma, or energy, stories about those industries get softer coverage.

twist.text: Journalists rarely investigate their own employer's parent company. The bias is structural, not individual.

climax.text: Understanding who owns a news outlet explains patterns in its coverage that individual bias can't.

punchline.text: Follow the ownership. It explains the coverage.

quiz.question: How does corporate ownership affect news coverage?
options: Parent company interests can soften coverage of related industries
